sources.title: TI SN74LVC1G125 product / exact SCEM639 behavioral model

assumptions: Source waveform has 2 ns edges and the declared amplitude/frequency; no real Y120 clock model.
10, 30 and 100 pF are load sensitivities, not extracted module/flex/probe capacitances.
Native R125 is 33 Ω; reference benches intentionally omit it. VDD is an ideal declared source.
limitations: Native PCB/schematic/BOM and frozen engine/runs are unchanged. No whole-board EM, thermal or boot solver is added.
Boundary supplies, stimulus, receiver/cable capacitance and off-state loads are declared assumptions. No PCB/package/flex transmission-line model is included.
No internal IC branch currents or temperatures are inferred. A modeled VDD-port current is a macro output, not a measured silicon current.
SCEM639 is a generic family-derived, datasheet-value macro labeled for this exact part; its typical 25 °C behavior does not establish process/temperature extremes or a qualified DPW package.
The older downloaded IBIS omits DPW package data; do not substitute another package invisibly.
No startup-through-zero qualification: VCC below 1.65 V is outside normal operation, and model formulas divide by VCC. Native OE is tied low, so real ramp behavior remains a separate requirement.
The exact macro was executed, but its undamped-reference output screening failed. Native R125 damping does not qualify that reference or cure the vendor model.

SCEM639 output LOUT is parallel to the behavioral output conductance. With a 15 pF undamped load, stored ngspice results ring beyond the declared screening envelope. Simulator cross-check or a vendor-confirmed model is required before hardware decisions.
The 120 ns reference and 400 ns native-clock experiments use fixed valid operating supplies; neither is a cold-start simulation.

studies.summary: Original TI three-MOSFET LSF0102 macro uses the actual PCA9306 external 200 kΩ / 2.2 kΩ topology. Proxy results illustrate bus loading and back-bias mechanism only.

sources.title: TI PCA9306 datasheet, section 8.1.7 bias-current discussion
TI support supplies LSF0102 as a PCA9306-Q1 electrical proxy

assumptions: LSF0102 KP=22 mA/V² and VTO=0.7 V are unchanged vendor proxy parameters, not exact PCA9306 electrical characteristics.
Both bus sides use assumed lumped capacitance; the ideal 10 Ω open-drain sink is a stimulus, not a SoC/sensor IO model.

Absent-low-source cases use actual total 5 µF nominal local CAM_1V8 bypass but assume 1 GΩ/1 MΩ/100 kΩ residual loads and a 1 ms external 3.3 V ramp. These are sensitivity cases, not proposed PCB changes.
limitations: Native PCB/schematic/BOM and frozen engine/runs are unchanged. No whole-board EM, thermal or boot solver is added.
Boundary supplies, stimulus, receiver/cable capacitance and off-state loads are declared assumptions. No PCB/package/flex transmission-line model is included.
No internal IC branch currents or temperatures are inferred. A modeled VDD-port current is a macro output, not a measured silicon current.
Exact PCA9306 HSPICE is encrypted and not executed; its supplied TSSOP package also differs from DQE.
The three-MOSFET proxy omits characterized package parasitics, leakage corners, temperature limits, actual external regulator and peripheral off-state loads.
No I2C firmware/address/transaction emulation, maximum-clock qualification or authoritative bleed selection is claimed.

studies.title: SN74LVC1G125 revision comparison: v2 failure and v1 bounded screens
studies.summary: At identical controlled stimuli, v2 fails the output screen and v1 passes the bounded output/delay screens. Both use 1.8/3.3 V supplies, same-amplitude 25 MHz input with 2 ns edges, and 15 pF external load. These comparative references do not reproduce every datasheet test condition or qualify the native board.

sources.title: TI SN74LVC1G125 SCEM639 original behavioral model
TI SN74LVC1G125 SCEM579 original PSpice model

assumptions: The 1 µΩ numerical connection approximates an omitted series resistor; 15 pF is the declared external load. The v1 macro also contains 30 pF of its own output capacitance.
Supply, stimulus and temperature assumptions match across both model revisions.
limitations: Two typical reference screens do not qualify the full voltage/process/temperature/receiver-load range or DPW package.

These use 25 MHz and ideal input sources; the datasheet timing figure specifies a repetition rate up to 10 MHz and a 50 Ω generator. At 3.3 V VCC the datasheet uses 3 V input and 1.5 V crossing; these comparisons use 3.3 V input and 1.65 V crossing. Timing-range comparisons are indicative, not datasheet test reproduction.
The v1 output dependent source has no complete VDD energy accounting. No v1 supply-current or thermal prediction is published.
No v1 cold-start, OE-ramp or real camera-line study is claimed. The v2 failure remains retained.
